<aside class="takeaways" aria-label="Key takeaways">

**Key takeaways**

- Hearth charges flat prices: $29 to $99 a month for plans capped at 5 to 15 users, or $199 a month for unlimited users.
- All seven alternatives have a free plan; paid plans start at $5 (Dogwood), $9 (Alder, Cedar), $10 (Elm, Fir, Ginkgo) and $11 (Birch) per user/month, billed yearly.
- Hearth’s Free plan covers 1 project and 3 users, and its capped paid plans top out at 15 users ($99 a month).
- Alder is the best pick for visual workflows and automation; Birch suits task dependencies, Fir client billing, Elm resource planning and Ginkgo documentation.

</aside>

Hearth is simple, clean, and gets the job done for small teams with straightforward projects. But when your workflows grow more complex, you start feeling the gaps — no custom fields, no advanced automation, limited reporting, and a price that climbs fast when you need more people.

Our team has set up planning tools for 120+ teams, many of them moving off simpler tools like Hearth. The most common problem? Teams outgrow the simplicity. They need custom workflows, visual project views, automation that goes beyond notifications, and fine-grained permissions.

This guide covers seven [Hearth alternatives](/planning-software/) — from visual work platforms to all-in-one workspaces — chosen for what teams actually need after hitting Hearth’s limits.

1.  [Quick Comparison: 7 Hearth Alternatives](#quick-comparison)

<a id="quick-comparison"></a>

## Quick Comparison: 7 Hearth Alternatives

| Tool | Best For | Starting Price (billed yearly) | Free Plan? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Alder** | Visual boards, automation, forms | $9/user/mo | ✅ Yes (up to 2 seats) |
| **Birch** | Task lists, timeline views | $11/user/mo | ✅ Yes (up to 2 users) |
| **Cedar** | Highly customizable, all-in-one | $9/user/mo (Core; classic plan $7) | ✅ Yes (unlimited members) |
| **Dogwood** | Kanban boards, simple workflows | $5/user/mo | ✅ Yes (10 boards, 10 collaborators) |
| **Elm** | Resource planning, Gantt charts | $10/user/mo | ✅ Yes (unlimited users, 200 active tasks) |
| **Fir** | Client projects, time tracking | $10/user/mo | ✅ Yes (up to 5 users) |
| **Ginkgo** | Docs + tasks, knowledge base | $10/user/mo | ✅ Yes (individuals; limited blocks for 2+ members) |

## What Makes These Alternatives Better Than Hearth?

Hearth is simple on purpose — flat pricing, few features, a focus on talking. But that simplicity becomes a limit once your projects need structure.

| What You Need | Why Hearth Falls Short | What Alternatives Offer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Custom workflows** | Fixed structure, no custom fields | Custom fields, statuses and views |
| **Visual project views** | Lists, card boards and schedules | Kanban, Gantt, calendar, workload charts |
| **Advanced automation** | Basic notifications only | Trigger-based workflows, cross-project automation |
| **Detailed reporting** | Minimal built-in reports | Time tracking, resource planning, custom dashboards |

Hearth charges flat monthly prices: $29 to $99 for plans capped at 5 to 15 users, or $199 a month for unlimited users and projects.

<aside class="sidenote sidenote--def"><p class="sidenote__label">Definition</p><p><strong>Flat pricing:</strong> one monthly price for the whole account instead of a price per user. Hearth caps users and projects on its $29 to $99 plans; the $199 plan removes both caps.</p></aside>

<a id="alder"></a>

## 1\. Alder — Best for Visual Workflows & Automation

**Why teams choose it:** [Alder](/alder/review/) replaces Hearth’s simplicity with visual flexibility. Instead of one fixed layout, you build boards with the columns your work needs and switch between views.

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Custom boards** | Many column types (status, date, people, dropdown, formulas) |
| **Multiple views** | Kanban, Gantt, calendar, timeline, workload, map views |
| **Automation** | Recipes for status changes, notifications and repeating tasks (250 actions/month on the middle plan) |
| **Forms** | Public forms that create items |

### What Alder Does Better Than Hearth

| Capability | Alder | Hearth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Custom fields** | ✅ Unlimited types | ❌ Fixed structure |
| **Visual views** | ✅ Kanban, Gantt, calendar, workload and more | ⚠️ Lists, card boards, schedules |
| **Automation** | ✅ 250 actions/month and up | ❌ Basic notifications |
| **Integrations** | ✅ Hundreds of apps | ⚠️ A few connectors |

### Pros & Cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ Highly visual and easy to learn | ❌ Can get expensive for large teams |
| ✅ Strong automation and integrations | ❌ Learning curve for advanced features |
| ✅ Pricing tiers for different needs | ❌ Forms only create items (don’t update) |
| ✅ Phone apps on every plan | ❌ Reporting limited on lower tiers |

### Example Use Case

Consider a clinic group using Hearth to plan new-patient onboarding across many sites. It hits a wall when it needs to track appointment statuses, team assignments and document approvals.

On Alder, it could build boards with coloured status columns for each stage, send reminders when documents wait for review, and give site managers a view of their team’s workload at a glance.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 (up to 2 seats) | One or two people trying it |
| Basic | $9/user/mo | Small teams, basic boards |
| Standard | $12/user/mo | Automation, timeline views |
| Pro | $19/user/mo | Time tracking, formulas, dashboards |

*Billed annually (yearly billing saves 18%); 3-seat minimum.*

### When to Choose Alder Over Hearth

-   You need visual tracking with Gantt charts, Kanban boards or workload views
-   Your workflows need custom fields and automation
-   You’re running projects across teams, with dependencies
-   You want forms that feed straight into project boards

**Ready to move beyond Hearth’s limits?** [Contact us for a free 30-minute call](/contact-us/) to see how Alder can replace your current set-up.

<a id="birch"></a>

## 2\. Birch — Best for Task-Centric Teams

**Why teams choose it:** Birch is built around tasks. If Hearth’s lists feel too loose, Birch gives every task an owner, a date and the tasks it waits on.

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Task dependencies** | Link tasks so later work waits for earlier work |
| **Timeline view** | Gantt-style timeline with drag-and-drop scheduling |
| **Portfolios** | Roll many projects up into one view |
| **Custom fields** | Add dropdowns, numbers, dates and text to any task |

### What Birch Does Better Than Hearth

| Capability | Birch | Hearth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Task dependencies** | ✅ Built in | ❌ Not available |
| **Portfolio views** | ✅ Multi-project dashboards | ❌ One project at a time |
| **Search** | ✅ Saved searches, filters | ❌ Basic search |
| **Guest access** | ✅ Fine-grained permissions | ⚠️ Admin controls only on the top plan |

### Pros & Cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ Excellent task management with subtasks and dependencies | ❌ Fewer chat features than Hearth |
| ✅ Timeline view for scheduling | ❌ Automation starts on the first paid plan |
| ✅ Free plan for up to 2 users | ❌ Reporting needs a paid plan |
| ✅ Clean, calm interface | ❌ Time tracking only on the higher plan |

### Example Use Case

Consider a product team whose launches slip because one late task holds up five others, and Hearth cannot show which.

In Birch, each task names what it waits on, and the timeline shows the knock-on effect of a late one before the launch date moves.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal | $0 (up to 2 users) | One or two people, basic tasks |
| Starter | $11/user/mo | Timeline, custom fields |
| Advanced | $25/user/mo | Portfolios, automation, reporting |

*Billed annually.*

### When to Choose Birch Over Hearth

-   Your projects have complex task dependencies
-   You need a view across many projects
-   Owners and deadlines matter more than team chat
-   You want a calmer interface than Alder

<a id="cedar"></a>

## 3\. Cedar — Best for Feature-Rich Customization

**Why teams choose it:** Cedar tries to be everything at once: tasks, docs, goals, chat and whiteboards. If Hearth left you with five other tools on the side, Cedar can replace most of them.

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Docs** | Shared docs linked to tasks (instead of Hearth’s message board) |
| **Custom views** | List, board, Gantt, calendar, workload, table, map, timeline and more |
| **Goals** | Track team goals with measurable targets |
| **Automations** | Status changes, assignments, notifications: 100 a month on Free, 1,000 on Core |

### What Cedar Does Better Than Hearth

| Capability | Cedar | Hearth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Custom views** | ✅ Many view types | ⚠️ Lists, card boards, schedules |
| **Free plan** | ✅ Unlimited members | ⚠️ 1 project, 3 users |
| **Goals** | ✅ Built in | ❌ Not available |
| **Whiteboards** | ✅ Built in | ❌ Not available |

### Pros & Cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ Very feature-rich (docs, goals, chat, whiteboards) | ❌ A lot for new users — steep learning curve |
| ✅ Free plan with unlimited members | ❌ Free plan storage is small |
| ✅ Many ways to customise | ❌ Two plan lineups (current and classic) to compare |
| ✅ Strong automation and integrations | ❌ So much choice that set-up takes time |

### Example Use Case

Consider an events company that keeps tasks in Hearth, budgets in spreadsheets and run sheets in a docs app.

In Cedar, each event is one space with its tasks, its budget fields and its run sheet side by side.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 (unlimited members, small storage) | Small teams trying it |
| Core | $9/user/mo | Unlimited storage, Gantt, custom fields |
| Business | $17/user/mo | Resource planning, timesheets |

*Billed annually.*

### When to Choose Cedar Over Hearth

-   You want to bring many tools into one
-   Your team needs docs, tasks, goals and chat in one place
-   You value deep customisation over simplicity
-   You want a free plan for unlimited members

## 4\. Dogwood — Best for Kanban-Style Simplicity

**Why teams choose it:** Dogwood is Hearth’s opposite — pure visual simplicity. If Hearth’s message boards feel cluttered and you just want to see cards moving across columns, Dogwood does exactly that.

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Boards and cards** | Columns of cards you drag from stage to stage |
| **Checklists** | Steps inside each card |
| **Automation** | Rules and buttons on every plan |
| **Power-ups** | Add calendars, fields and integrations to a board |

### What Dogwood Does Better Than Hearth

| Capability | Dogwood | Hearth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Visual workflow** | ✅ Kanban at the centre | ⚠️ Card boards on the side |
| **Ease of use** | ✅ Learned in minutes | ✅ Also simple |
| **Automation** | ✅ On every plan | ❌ Basic notifications |
| **Price to start** | ✅ $5/user/mo | ⚠️ Flat monthly price |

### Pros & Cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ The simplest tool here | ❌ No dependencies of its own |
| ✅ Automation on every plan | ❌ Large boards get crowded |
| ✅ Cheap to start | ❌ Reporting needs the top plan |
| ✅ Many add-ons | ❌ No time tracking of its own |

### Example Use Case

Consider a marketing agency running 15 client campaigns that struggled with Hearth’s chat-first design. It needed to see campaign stages at a glance — pitching, writing, review, publishing.

Dogwood boards would give each client a visual pipeline. Cards move from “Drafting” to “Client Review” to “Approved” with a simple drag, with due dates, attachments and checklists on each card.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 (10 boards) | Individuals, small teams |
| Standard | $5/user/mo | Unlimited boards, custom fields |
| Premium | $10/user/mo | More views, unlimited automation |

*Billed annually. Monthly billing available.*

### When to Choose Dogwood Over Hearth

-   You want pure visual simplicity without extra features
-   Your workflows fit columns of moving cards
-   You want automation on every plan
-   You prefer free tools with pay-as-you-grow pricing

<a id="elm"></a>

## 5\. Elm — Best for Resource Management

**Why teams choose it:** Elm is the enterprise-grade alternative to Hearth — built for teams that need resource planning, workload balancing and detailed reporting.

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Workload view** | See who is overloaded and who has room |
| **Gantt charts** | Dependencies and the critical path |
| **Request forms** | Intake forms that start projects |
| **Approvals** | Review and sign-off steps built into tasks |

### What Elm Does Better Than Hearth

| Capability | Elm | Hearth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Resource planning** | ✅ Workload and capacity | ❌ Not available |
| **Reporting** | ✅ Cross-project reports | ❌ Minimal |
| **Approvals** | ✅ Built in | ⚠️ By hand in comments |
| **Time tracking** | ✅ Business plan and up | ❌ Not available |

### Pros & Cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ Strong resource planning | ❌ Expensive at the top |
| ✅ Detailed reports | ❌ Takes time to set up |
| ✅ Approvals built in | ❌ Busy interface |
| ✅ Scales to large teams | ❌ Top plans are quote-only |

### Example Use Case

Consider a finance firm running several audit projects at once. Hearth shows the tasks, but not who is drowning in work while others are idle.

Elm’s workload view shows each person’s hours across every project, so managers can move work before deadlines slip.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 (unlimited users, 200 active tasks) | Trying it |
| Team | $10/user/mo | Gantt, dashboards |
| Business | $25/user/mo | Workload, time tracking, approvals |

*Billed annually; the top plans are quote-only.*

### When to Choose Elm Over Hearth

-   You need to plan resources across many projects
-   Your team has 20 or more people
-   You need detailed reporting and time tracking
-   Approval steps are central to your work

**Need help choosing between these alternatives?** [Contact us for a free call](/contact-us/) — our team has set up planning tools for 120 teams.

<a id="fir"></a>

## 6\. Fir — Best for Client Project Management

**Why teams choose it:** Fir is built for agencies and consultancies running client projects. If Hearth’s flat structure does not separate internal work from billable work, Fir does.

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Time tracking** | Billable hours logged on each task |
| **Budgets** | Time and money budgets per project |
| **Client users** | Clients see their own projects only |
| **Invoices** | Invoices built from logged time |

### What Fir Does Better Than Hearth

| Capability | Fir | Hearth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Billable time** | ✅ Built in | ❌ Not available |
| **Profit per project** | ✅ Budget vs. actual | ❌ Not available |
| **Client access** | ✅ Limited client users | ⚠️ Clients see a lot |
| **Invoicing** | ✅ From logged time | ❌ Not available |

### Pros & Cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ Made for agencies | ❌ Less suited to internal teams |
| ✅ Time and budgets in one place | ❌ Fewer views than Alder |
| ✅ Clear client access | ❌ Invoicing only on higher plans |
| ✅ Free plan for 5 users | ❌ Smaller app catalogue |

### Example Use Case

Consider a design agency with a dozen clients that exports time logs from a separate timer, matches them to projects in spreadsheets and emails status updates every week.

In Fir, designers log time on the task itself, budgets update as they go, and clients see progress in their own view.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 (up to 5 users) | Small agencies |
| Deliver | $10/user/mo | Time tracking, client users |
| Grow | $25/user/mo | Budgets, workload, invoices |

*Billed annually (yearly billing saves 20%).*

### When to Choose Fir Over Hearth

-   You run an agency or consultancy with client projects
-   Time tracking and profit matter
-   You need client users with limited access
-   You bill clients by the hour or by milestone

## 7\. Ginkgo — Best for Knowledge Management + Tasks

**Why teams choose it:** Ginkgo blurs the line between wiki, knowledge base and project plan. If Hearth’s chat-heavy approach does not keep what your team knows, Ginkgo keeps it next to the work.

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Pages and databases** | Docs that hold task tables |
| **Wikis** | A team handbook with verified pages |
| **Templates** | Ready-made layouts for plans and notes |
| **Automations** | Database automations on paid plans |

### What Ginkgo Does Better Than Hearth

| Capability | Ginkgo | Hearth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Knowledge base** | ✅ Built in | ❌ Not available |
| **Flexible docs** | ✅ Pages inside pages | ⚠️ Simple documents |
| **Databases** | ✅ Tables, boards, timelines | ❌ Not available |
| **Templates** | ✅ Large gallery | ⚠️ A few |

### Pros & Cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ Docs and tasks in one place | ❌ Learning curve for deep set-ups |
| ✅ Very flexible | ❌ Weaker for strict project control |
| ✅ Great for wikis | ❌ Limited blocks for teams on Free |
| ✅ Clean writing experience | ❌ Few reports |

### Example Use Case

Consider a software startup whose specs, docs and tasks lived in three tools, with Hearth as one of them. Context was lost between them.

They moved everything into Ginkgo — roadmaps with task tables inside, specs linked to features, and sprint plans next to the technical notes. The team stopped asking where things were.

### Pricing

| Plan | Price | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 (individuals) | Personal notes |
| Plus | $10/user/mo | Small teams |
| Business | $15/user/mo | Larger teams, more control |

*Billed annually (yearly billing saves up to 20%).*

### When to Choose Ginkgo Over Hearth

-   You need a knowledge base as much as task management
-   Your team values flexible docs and wikis
-   You want one tool for documentation + projects
-   You’re fine with a learning curve for deep customisation

## Example Migrations: Teams Outgrowing Hearth

### Example 1: Clinic Operations Team

**The Hearth Problem:** A group of clinics uses Hearth to plan new-patient onboarding across its sites. Lists show what needs to happen but not *who* is overloaded, and nothing reminds anyone of a waiting document.

<div class="facts">

**The Migration:** Move to **Alder** to get:

-   Coloured status columns showing each patient’s onboarding stage
-   Workload views showing which coordinators are overloaded
-   Automations sending reminders when documents sit in “Pending Review” for 48+ hours

</div>

**The Result:** Clinic managers see progress without asking, and coordinators spend less time on manual updates.

### Example 2: Design Agency

**The Hearth Problem:** A design agency with 15 clients needs better time tracking, profit per project and client access. Hearth’s flat price is fine, but the team exports time logs by hand every week.

<div class="facts">

**The Migration:** Move to **Fir** to get:

-   Time tracking on the task itself (no separate tool)
-   Budget vs. actual reports showing which projects make money
-   Client users who see their projects without the agency’s internal boards

</div>

**The Result:** Billing takes less time, and the agency can see which clients are profitable.

### Example 3: Retail Operations

**The Hearth Problem:** A shop chain opening new stores uses Hearth for tasks, spreadsheets for budgets, a board tool for visual tasks and a separate timer for contractors.

<div class="facts">

**The Migration:** Move to **Cedar** to bring together:

-   Task boards for building and set-up progress
-   Custom fields for budgets, contractor hours and inspections
-   Docs for store-opening manuals and checklists
-   Time tracking for contractor invoices

</div>

**The Result:** Fewer tools to pay for and look after, in exchange for a longer set-up than Hearth.

## How to Choose the Right Hearth Alternative

### Decision Matrix

| If You Need… | Choose This | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visual workflows + automation | **Alder** | Best balance of clear boards and automation |
| Task dependencies + timeline views | **Birch** | Made for task-centred project work |
| All-in-one | **Cedar** | Replace several tools with one customisable platform |
| Pure Kanban simplicity | **Dogwood** | The cleanest visual boards |
| Resource and workload planning | **Elm** | Enterprise-grade resource planning and reports |
| Client projects + time billing | **Fir** | Made for agencies and consultancies |
| Docs + tasks + knowledge base | **Ginkgo** | Best mix of wiki and task management |

### Key Questions to Ask Your Team

<div class="facts">

**1\. What broke in Hearth?**

-   Need custom fields? → Alder, Cedar, Birch
-   Need better reporting? → Elm, Fir, Alder
-   Need visual workflows? → Dogwood, Alder, Cedar
-   Need time tracking? → Fir, Cedar, Elm

**2\. How big is your team?**

-   2-10 people → Dogwood, Birch (free plans), Alder
-   10-50 people → Alder, Cedar, Birch
-   50+ people → Elm, Alder Pro

**3\. What’s your budget per user?**

-   Under $10/user/mo → Cedar, Dogwood, Alder Basic
-   $10-20/user/mo → Birch, Fir, Alder Standard
-   $20+/user/mo → Elm, enterprise tiers

**4\. How much complexity can you take?**

-   Low (want simplicity) → Dogwood, Birch
-   Medium (some customisation) → Alder, Fir
-   High (want deep flexibility) → Cedar, Ginkgo, Elm

</div>

## Add-Ons: Going Beyond a Tool’s Own Limits

Whichever tool you choose, you’ll eventually hit limits with its forms and its email automations. Many tools’ own forms can only *create* items — they can’t *update* existing ones. And their emails are often plain text with no CC or BCC.

**Add-ons from the tool’s marketplace** often fill these gaps:

| What the Tool Can’t Do | What an Add-On Can Do |
| --- | --- |
| Forms that update existing items | Each item gets its own form address. Answers write to that item — no duplicates. |
| CC/BCC on email automations | CC groups, rules for who is copied, and BCC on every automated email. |
| Rich HTML email | A full editor with merge fields, formatted like real business email. |
| Cross-board workflows | One trigger creates items on several boards or updates statuses across your workspace. |

Check what an add-on stores, where it stores it and who can see it before you connect it to your work.

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary><h3>Which Hearth alternatives like Alder and Cedar best manage custom workflows and multi-project views?</h3></summary>

Alder handles custom workflows with boards, many column types and automations (250 actions a month on its middle plan), and its dashboards combine data from several boards. Cedar supports nested lists, task dependencies and automations on every plan, with a steeper learning curve.

</details>

<details>
<summary><h3>How do I move task data from Hearth to Birch without losing dependencies or old comments?</h3></summary>

Export your Hearth projects, then rebuild them in Birch: map Hearth lists to Birch projects or sections and their items to tasks and subtasks, then add dependencies in Birch (Hearth has none to carry over). Check what happens to comments and attachments in a test project before you move everything.

</details>

<details>
<summary><h3>Which Hearth alternatives offer Gantt charts for complex scheduling?</h3></summary>

Among the tools in this guide: Alder has Gantt views from its middle plan; Birch has timeline views with dependencies from its first paid plan; Elm has Gantt charts on every paid plan; and Cedar includes them on Core. Hearth itself has schedules and card boards but no Gantt chart.

</details>

<details>
<summary><h3>Can Dogwood handle automation and custom fields to replace Hearth's limits in growing teams?</h3></summary>

Partly. Custom fields start on its first paid plan ($5 per user/month), and automation is on every plan, with a monthly limit on the free one. Dogwood still has no dependencies or time tracking of its own, so teams with complex projects usually look at Alder or Birch instead.

</details>

<details>
<summary><h3>Which Hearth alternatives include time tracking, invoicing and resource planning for agencies?</h3></summary>

Fir is the closest fit among the tools in this guide: billable time tracking starts on its first paid plan, and the next plan adds time budgets, workload planning and invoices from logged time. Elm adds time tracking and workload on its business plan.

</details>

<details>
<summary><h3>How does Elm's reporting compare to Hearth for tracking project profit and goals?</h3></summary>

Elm's reports pull data from many projects with filters and exports, and its higher plans add budgeting and links to business-intelligence tools. Hearth's own reporting is minimal, so teams that need profit or goal tracking usually add another tool or move to Elm or Fir.

</details>
